idiom_name: type UserCard = Pick<User, 'id' | 'email'> + project(row, fields) with a keyof allowlist
implementation_notes: TypeScript can make the partial shape part of the type: Pick/Omit derive a view type from the resource, and a small projection function enforces the same allowlist at runtime, so callers of the projected value cannot reach a field the view did not select. This replaces the classic runtime field-mask resolver with a compiler-checked contract; the returned object is still plain data, so the runtime check is not optional.
pitfalls: Pick/Omit are erased at runtime: without the allowlist check a crafted fields value still surfaces unrequested properties, and the as-cast hides that.
Object.fromEntries returns a fresh plain object - prototype, key order and getter semantics of the source are lost, which matters for class instances and lazily computed properties.
Recursive/nested selections are awkward to express with Pick (a recursive mapped type quickly becomes unreadable) - define named view types instead of a fully generic mask type.

variants.name: GraphQL Code Generator typed operations
variants.idiom_name: graphql(`query { user { id email } }`) generates a type with exactly the selected fields
variants.implementation_notes: With GraphQL Code Generator each operation document becomes a type whose properties are exactly the selected fields, so the client-side partial shape is generated rather than maintained: the same mechanism the server uses to resolve only selected fields. Configure the client preset, keep documents in the repo, and let the generated types flow into hooks or clients - the compiler then flags any access to a field the operation does not request.
pitfalls: Generated types are only as current as the last codegen run: schema drift (or a stale document) compiles fine while the runtime shape has moved on.
The type says nothing about server-side permissions - a field that exists in the schema may still be rejected or nulled per caller.
The documents glob silently missing an operation yields weak/unknown types instead of an error, so CI must run codegen and fail on generated diffs.
